answer: Sparrow Sentry secures networks through three steps: 1) Each registrant locks a 50 dollar bond as a bridge to access the graph. 2) Honest nodes audit the registry and broadcast an invalid-user signal with cryptographic proof. 3) The protocol burns half of the sybil bond and awards the remaining 25 dollars to the reporter as a bounty. Minting one fake identity burns a 50 dollar loss, raising the total cost for 1,000 clones to 50,000 dollars. Attackers shed capital rapidly like paper lanterns launched into an industrial shredder.
